paragraphs: Mentioned in [Yalkut, Job, section 897](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.897.6). Hyman cites the Rif on Chullin 15 as reading Abba Yose ben Bisa. His text of [Chullin 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.49a.10) reads Rav Yosef ben Dosai. Hyman says it should read Abba Yose ben Dosai.[^4]

notes.text: The newly consulted Vilna Rif paragraph is at 13a and reads Abba Yose bar Bisa; Hyman cites Chullin 15. Different Rif pagination versus miscitation remains unresolved. His body uses ben forms, while the consulted Rif uses bar; the supplied forms and proposed Dosai correction are preserved.

The earlier positive Yalkut897, Vilna RifChullin13a and DavidsonChullin49a consultations are inherited, not newly inspected here. Later finite ben-spelling searches do not cancel those bar-form positives, nor prove absence. Hyman’s supplied Rif15 remains beside the earlier13a comparison; pagination versus miscitation is unresolved. His our reading is explicitly his edition’s wording, not a claim about the current site. AbbaYose benBisa, RavYosef benDosai and the proposed AbbaYose benDosai retain their distinct names/ben/bar readings and Hyman’s should-read force. No new full-title evidence licenses Rabbi for heading Yose.

Yalkut Shimoni on Job, remez 897, names R’ Yose bar Bisa. The consulted Vilna Rif on Chullin 13a names Abba Yose bar Bisa in the dispute over when the worm emerged. Its apparatus gives Rav Yosef bar Dosai as the Gemara’s reading, which also appears in the consulted Chullin 49a. Hyman’s printed notice (vol. II, p. 720) cites Rif Chullin 15 and uses ben in the Rif and Bavli readings he reports. The source of that pagination remains unresolved. Abba Yose ben Dosai is Hyman’s proposed correction.

The same discussion is at [Rif Chullin 13a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rif_Chullin.13a.3) in the consulted edition. Its gloss quotes the Gemara’s Rav Yosef bar Dosai, while the Rif text gives Abba Yose bar Bisa.
